subject: CobaltBank: sustained latency/errors on reserved pool — immediate mitigation
messages:
From: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cobaltbank.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anjali Shah <anjali.shah@cobaltbank.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T09:15:00Z
Subject: Urgent — sustained latency + 5xx errors on our reserved pool (CobaltBank)

Rishi,

We started seeing a sustained increase in tail latency and a rising 5xx rate against our reserved-capacity endpoints ~09:00 UTC. Throughput (QPS) dropped by ~30% while the request queue depth increased sharply — users are seeing request timeouts and a handful of production failures. This is affecting our payments reconciliation flow (high priority).

Key details:
- Impact window: ~09:02–09:25 UTC
- Approx 18k requests queued at peak, headroom consumed on our reserved pool
- Error surface: 500/502 responses and a small number of token truncations

We opened a ticket but this needs an immediate mitigation plan. Please advise: can you fall back any endpoints to hosted models or temporarily increase our reserved headroom? We need an estimated ETA for a fix and whether Redwood can cover any SLO credits if this persists.

Attached: sample_request_ids.txt (sent via ticket)

—Samir
Head of Platform, CobaltBank

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cobaltbank.com>
Cc: Anjali Shah <anjali.shah@cobaltbank.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-02T09:26:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent — sustained latency + 5xx errors on our reserved pool (CobaltBank)

Samir — thanks for the heads up and apologies for the disruption. We're on it. Quick plan:

1) I'm scheduling an immediate ops bridge (link below) with infra and our Reserved pool owners.
2) Naomi — can you pull pool utilization, queue depth, and recent scheduling decisions for the CobaltBank reservation (09:00–09:40 UTC)? Attach any short csv/plots.
3) If we confirm pool saturation, two immediate mitigations we can do within 10–20 minutes:
   - Route lower-risk endpoints to hosted inference variants (less latency-sensitive routes)
   - Temporarily grant overbooked headroom to CobaltBank (emergency uplift) while we remove the spike source
\Samir — will you share 1–2 sample request IDs and the ticket link so we can trace? Also confirm if a partial fallback (read-only or non-prod endpoints) is acceptable short-term.

Proposed call: 09:45 UTC (15 minutes) — joining: Naomi (infra), Marissa (customer ops), Vivek (lead eng)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-02T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent — sustained latency + 5xx errors on our reserved pool (CobaltBank) — initial diagnostics

Rishi / team — quick diagnostic attached. See pool_metrics_20280402.csv and kv_cache_hitrates.png. TL;DR: evidence points at sustained saturation of the dedicated GPU pool that backs DB-9482 (CobaltBank). Details below.

Observations:
- GPU utilization across pool: 92–99% between 08:55–09:30 UTC (consistent with saturation).
- Token generation latency (p50/p95/p99): normal at p50, p95 jumped from 180ms -> 650ms, p99 to ~1.8s during spike window.
- Queue depth: baseline 200–400; peaked at ~18k (matching customer report).
- KV cache hit-rate for CobaltBank models fell from 78% -> 22% at 09:05 (we saw a cache flush event traced to a large batch load from another tenant at 09:03 UTC).
- No node-level OOMs; kernel retries present but not dominant.

Immediate recommended actions (short horizon):
1) Block the noisy batch load (originating tenant id: t-7319) — already flagged to runtime team, ETA 8–12 minutes to abort in-flight batches.
2) Enable emergency uplift for CobaltBank +20% reserved qps (config change) — requires approval from product/finance for temporary billing override. We can program it in ~7 minutes once approved.
3) Apply selective routing: non-critical endpoints -> hosted fallback (we have the route config ready, needs one-click from ops).

Attachments: pool_metrics_20280402.csv (CSV), kv_cache_hitrates.png (PNG)

Naomi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-02T11:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent — sustained latency + 5xx errors on our reserved pool (CobaltBank) — exec decision needed

Team — thanks Naomi, that aligns with what I was expecting. This has moved into an exec-level decision: short-term cost vs. customer impact. Two pragmatic options:

A) Emergency uplift (preferred): grant CobaltBank +20% reserved throughput immediately, bill as overage with a temporary credit discussion post-incident. Impact: service restored, minimal product-surface changes, cost to Redwood ~estimated $3k/hr while active. We need Product/Finance OK to proceed immediately and an SLA credit cadence if sustained.

B) Route to hosted fallback for non-critical endpoints (low cost): requires customer consent for the endpoints and results in slightly higher p99 for those routes but immediate relief. This is lower cost but exposes CobaltBank to potential consistency differences.

I'm authorizing ops to prepare the config change for A; Rishi — I need a firm OK from you to trigger uplift and inform Samir with a clear timeline and cost note. If you prefer B as primary, notify me and we'll prepare messaging and partial fallback mapping.

Attachment: emergency_capacity_plan.pdf

Marissa
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cobaltbank.com>, Anjali Shah <anjali.shah@cobaltbank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-02T13:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent — sustained latency + 5xx errors on our reserved pool (CobaltBank) — next steps and 13:00 UTC bridge

Samir / Anjali — thank you for the samples and patience. Quick update and immediate next steps: 

- Root cause: transient cache flush from a large batch load at 09:03 UTC that briefly dropped hit rates and drove queueing. Naomi's diagnostics attached.
- Immediate mitigation (in progress): Naomi/ops will abort the noisy batch and we will apply a +20% emergency uplift to your reservation. Ops estimates this will be in place within 12 minutes of approval.
- Alternate fallback: if you prefer, we can route lower-risk endpoints to hosted models to reduce pressure while we remediate — choose this if you want to avoid temporary billing differences.

Marissa has authorized preparing the uplift config. Marissa — please confirm and I'll send the authorization to Finance for fast-track approval.

Bridge scheduled: 13:00 UTC (meeting link: https://meet.redwood.ai/ops-call/rishi-cobaltbank-20280402)
